lead.headline: CYCLONE MURASU: RED ALERT FOR FIVE ANDHRA DISTRICTS
lead.deck: The storm is forecast to cross the south Andhra coast near Nellore and Narsapur on Tuesday; extreme rain is likely today
paragraphs: The India Meteorological Department has issued a red alert for extremely heavy rain on Monday in Krishna, Guntur, Bapatla, Prakasam and Nellore districts as Cyclone Murasu approaches the Andhra Pradesh coast.

The storm is forecast to cross between Nellore and Narsapur from late Monday night into the early hours of Tuesday as a severe cyclonic storm, with sustained winds of 100–110 km/h and gusts up to 120 km/h. Authorities have urged residents to follow local instructions.
The warning covers a different system from last week’s Cyclone Arnab. Forecasts can change; residents should follow the latest IMD bulletins and district advisories.

sidebarStory.headline: KARNATAKA PREPARES ORDER ON KANNADA FLAG FOR PRIVATE INSTITUTIONS
sidebarStory.subhead: The state says it will prepare a legal framework for official recognition of the red-and-yellow flag
paragraphs: Deputy Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar said the government plans to issue an order this month asking private institutions to hoist the Kannada flag. He said the proposal, including rules for institutions receiving government support, would be discussed ahead of the winter session.

stories.headline: WARD ONE DRIVE BEGINS IN SIX CENTRAL BENGALURU WARDS
stories.deck: Around 200 personnel have been deployed for repairs and clean-up work
paragraphs: The first Ward One campaign covered six wards, from New Thippasandra to Chamarajpet, with about 200 personnel, 33 tractors, 17 tippers and eight JCBs. Work includes pothole filling, footpath repairs, drain cleaning, streetlight maintenance and removal of encroachments.

stories.headline: FILES BEING PREPARED TO WITHDRAW CASES AGAINST KANNADA ACTIVISTS
paragraphs: Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar said files were being prepared to withdraw cases against Kannada activists, while warning pro-Kannada groups against attacking IT companies or taking the law into their own hands.

stories.headline: HMT LAUNCHES EIGHT KANNADIGA WATCH DESIGNS FOR RAJYOTSAVA
paragraphs: HMT introduced eight Kannadiga watch models for Karnataka Rajyotsava, with reported prices ranging from ₹3,500 to ₹3,600.

groups.ariaLabel: India politics, economy, and weather news

stories.headline: OPPOSITION RALLY RENEWS DEMAND FOR ELECTION CHIEF’S RESIGNATION
stories.deck: Tens of thousands gathered in Delhi over the voter-roll revision; the Election Commission says the exercise removes duplicate and ineligible entries
paragraphs: Opposition parties in the INDIA bloc held a rally at Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan on Sunday, calling for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to resign over the contentious revision of electoral rolls. The Associated Press reported that tens of thousands attended.

Rahul Gandhi and other leaders said the review risks disenfranchising voters. The Election Commission and the government reject claims of political bias, saying the process is intended to remove duplicate and ineligible entries.

stories.headline: IDBI BANK STRIKE NOTICE COVERS NOVEMBER 2 AND 3
paragraphs: IDBI Bank has advised customers of a proposed two-day employee strike. Branch-based services may be affected depending on participation; the bank says digital channels, ATMs and customer service points are to remain available.

stories.headline: FOUR-DAY RENEWABLE ENERGY SUMMIT OPENS IN DELHI
paragraphs: The Bharat Renewable Energy Summit and Expo runs November 2–5 at Bharat Mandapam. The Prime Minister’s Office says participants from more than 130 countries are expected, with the opening address scheduled for Monday afternoon.

stories.headline: BENGALURU MARKS KANNADA RAJYOTSAVA WITH RED-AND-YELLOW DISPLAY
stories.deck: Students, teachers and education officials gathered at Kanteerava Stadium for the state’s 71st formation-day celebrations
paragraphs: The Kanteerava Stadium event drew a large crowd for Karnataka’s 71st Rajyotsava, with students forming the main contingent and the venue decorated in the colours of the Kannada flag.

stories.headline: BELLANDUR RESIDENTS BRING KARNATAKA FOLK TRADITIONS TO APARTMENT FESTIVAL
paragraphs: More than 100 folk artists from several Karnataka districts performed at a Bellandur apartment community’s Rajyotsava celebration, organised by its Kannada Sangha.

stories.headline: CLOUDY SKY, OCCASIONAL SHOWERS FORECAST FOR MONDAY
paragraphs: Bengaluru is forecast to see occasional rain or thundershowers, with a high near 30°C and a low near 20°C, according to Monday’s city forecast.

stories.headline: ANDHRA COASTAL WATCH
stories.deck: Follow IMD bulletins and district instructions as forecasts are updated.
paragraphs: Five districts are under a red alert for extremely heavy rain today. Murasu is forecast to cross the south Andhra coast early Tuesday.
